overview: Benin's femtech scene is small but visible, anchored by a handful of founder-led digital health ventures out of Cotonou such as Dotoh (teleconsultation for underserved women), ELLES (cycle and contraception tracking) and KEA Medicals (universal medical ID). The policy backdrop is notable: Benin passed one of West Africa's most liberal abortion laws in 2021, permitting termination on request up to 12 weeks. Maternal mortality remains very high and modern contraceptive use low, framing the demand for women's health innovation. International backers (UNICEF, Sweden, the Tony Elumelu Foundation) rather than local capital drive most funding, and dedicated gender-lens capital for Benin is scarce.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: The biggest recent signal came from an international platform selecting a Beninese women's health startup, alongside a Cotonou-hosted health tech event.

items.text: Benin's Dotoh named in the first cohort of UNICEF Femtech Ventures, selected from over 1,100 applications across 85 countries, each startup eligible for up to USD 100,000 equity-free plus a year of technical support.

MTN Innovation Lab in Cotonou hosted the Africa HealthTech Export 2025 Bootcamp (17-21 Nov), gathering digital health startups, investors and regulators from Cote d'Ivoire, Senegal, Togo and beyond, with sessions on the UEMOA regulatory environment for digital medical devices.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Benin's reproductive health policy is unusually progressive for the region, most notably its liberalized abortion law.

items.text: Law No. 2021-12 modified the 2003 sexual and reproductive health law to authorize abortion on request up to 12 weeks, including in cases of material, educational, professional or moral distress, one of West Africa's most liberal frameworks.
The implementing decree (12 April 2023) was adopted, definitively establishing the operational legal framework for abortion access in Benin.
Government's Programme d'Action (Benin Revele) includes promotion and development of e-health as a national priority, underpinning digital health initiatives.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Ecosystem activity centers on Cotonou-based accelerators and founder-led health apps rather than large institutional programs.

items.text: MTN Innovation Lab (Cotonou) runs a startup acceleration programme, moving cohorts through mid-term evaluations and an annual Open Day, and hosted the 2025 Africa HealthTech Export bootcamp.
Seme City, the state-backed innovation and knowledge city launched in 2017, provides research labs, incubation and coworking space that supports health-related innovation.
ELLES, a women's cycle-tracking and contraception-information app, was created in 2022 by a group of young Beninese doctors led by Dr Viviane Oke.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Funding for Benin's women's health ventures is dominated by equity-free grants and accelerator awards from international bodies, not local venture capital.
